imo-isl-2018-a1.prompt:
Let $\mathbb Q_{>0}$ denote the set of all positive rational numbers. Determine all functions $f:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb Q_{>0}$ satisfying
$$f\big(x^2f(y)^2\big)=f(x)^2f(y)$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$.
imo-isl-2018-a1.answer: Only $f(x)=1$ for all $x$ (swap the roles of $f(a)$ and $f(b)$ to get $f(f(a))^2=Cf(a)$; then $f(a)/C$ is a $2^n$-th power of a rational for every $n$, so it equals $1$).

imo-isl-2018-a3.answer: Proof: discard $1$ and list $S=\{x_1<x_2<\dots\}$. If $x_{n+1}\ge 2x_n$ always, the reciprocal sums are bounded below $1$ (or are dyadic), giving (2). Otherwise $x_{n+1}<2x_n$ for some $n$; then $r=\frac1{x_n}-\frac1{x_{n+1}}$ is either not representable (2), or $r=\sum_{F_0}$ and $F_0\cup\{x_{n+1}\}$, $\{x_n\}$ give (1).

imo-isl-2018-a4.prompt:
Let $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots$ be a sequence of real numbers such that $a_0=0$, $a_1=1$, and for every $n\ge2$ there exists $1\le k\le n$ satisfying
$$a_n=\frac{a_{n-1}+\dots+a_{n-k}}{k}.$$
Find the maximal possible value of $a_{2018}-a_{2017}$.

imo-isl-2018-a5.prompt:
Determine all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\left(x+\frac1x\right)f(y)=f(xy)+f\!\left(\frac yx\right)$$
for all $x,y>0$.
imo-isl-2018-a5.answer: $f(x)=C_1x+\dfrac{C_2}{x}$ for arbitrary real constants $C_1,C_2$ (four substitutions give a linear system from which $f(t)$ is expressed as $\alpha t+\beta/t$).

imo-isl-2018-a6.prompt:
Let $m,n\ge2$ be integers. Let $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ be a polynomial with real coefficients such that
$$f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\left\lfloor\frac{x_1+\dots+x_n}{m}\right\rfloor\quad\text{for every }x_1,\dots,x_n\in\{0,1,\dots,m-1\}.$$
Prove that the total degree of $f$ is at least $n$.
imo-isl-2018-a6.answer: Proof: a finite-difference lemma shows that if $F(x_1,\dots,x_n)=G(x_1+\dots+x_n)$ on a grid $\prod\{0,\dots,a_i\}$ with $\deg G\le\sum a_i$, then $\deg F\ge\deg G$. Apply it with the interpolating polynomial $g$ of $\lfloor x/m\rfloor$ on $\{0,\dots,n(m-1)\}$; $g(x+m)-g(x)-1$ has $(n-1)(m-1)$ roots, so $\deg g\ge(n-1)(m-1)+1\ge n$.

imo-isl-2018-a7.prompt:
Find the maximal value of
$$S=\sqrt[3]{\frac a{b+7}}+\sqrt[3]{\frac b{c+7}}+\sqrt[3]{\frac c{d+7}}+\sqrt[3]{\frac d{a+7}},$$
where $a,b,c,d$ are nonnegative real numbers which satisfy $a+b+c+d=100$.

imo-isl-2018-c1.prompt: Let $n\ge3$ be an integer. Prove that there exists a set $S$ of $2n$ positive integers satisfying the following property: For every $m=2,3,\dots,n$ the set $S$ can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sums of elements, with one of subsets of cardinality $m$.
imo-isl-2018-c1.answer: Construction: $S=\{3^k,\,2\cdot3^k:1\le k\le n-1\}\cup\{1,\frac{3^n+9}2-1\}$ has sum $2\cdot3^n$, and $A_m=\{2\cdot3^k:n-m+1\le k\le n-1\}\cup\{3^{n-m+1}\}$ has $m$ elements and sum $3^n$.

imo-isl-2018-c2.prompt:
Queenie and Horst play a game on a $20\times20$ chessboard. In the beginning the board is empty. In every turn, Horst places a black knight on an empty square in such a way that his new knight does not attack any previous knights. Then Queenie places a white queen on an empty square. The game gets finished when somebody cannot move.

Find the maximal positive $K$ such that, regardless of the strategy of Queenie, Horst can put at least $K$ knights on the board.

imo-isl-2018-c3.prompt:
Let $n$ be a given positive integer. Sisyphus performs a sequence of turns on a board consisting of $n+1$ squares in a row, numbered $0$ to $n$ from left to right. Initially, $n$ stones are put into square $0$, and the other squares are empty. At every turn, Sisyphus chooses any nonempty square, say with $k$ stones, takes one of those stones and moves it to the right by at most $k$ squares (the stone should stay within the board). Sisyphus' aim is to move all $n$ stones to square $n$.

Prove that Sisyphus cannot reach the aim in less than
$$\left\lceil\frac n1\right\rceil+\left\lceil\frac n2\right\rceil+\left\lceil\frac n3\right\rceil+\dots+\left\lceil\frac nn\right\rceil$$
turns. (As usual, $\lceil x\rceil$ stands for the least integer not smaller than $x$.)
imo-isl-2018-c3.answer: Proof: number the stones $1,\dots,n$ and always move the highest-numbered stone of the chosen square. Then stone $k$ is only moved from squares with at most $k$ stones, so it moves at most $k$ squares per turn and needs at least $\lceil n/k\rceil$ turns.

imo-isl-2018-c5.prompt: Let $k$ be a positive integer. The organising committee of a tennis tournament is to schedule the matches for $2k$ players so that every two players play once, each day exactly one match is played, and each player arrives to the tournament site the day of his first match, and departs the day of his last match. For every day a player is present on the tournament, the committee has to pay $1$ coin to the hotel. The organisers want to design the schedule so as to minimise the total cost of all players' stays. Determine this minimum cost.
imo-isl-2018-c5.answer: $\dfrac{k(4k^2+k-1)}2$ coins (bound each sorted stay $e_{i+1}-b_{i+1}+1$ by counting matches that can happen before the $(i+1)$-th arrival and after the $(i+1)$-th-last departure; a two-group schedule attains all bounds).

imo-isl-2018-c6.prompt:
Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct positive integers. The following infinite process takes place on an initially empty board.

(i) If there is at least a pair of equal numbers on the board, we choose such a pair and increase one of its components by $a$ and the other by $b$.

(ii) If no such pair exists, we write down two times the number $0$.

Prove that, no matter how we make the choices in (i), operation (ii) will be performed only finitely many times.
imo-isl-2018-c6.answer: Proof: let $f(k)$ count how many times $k$ has appeared when (ii) is about to be applied for the $(N+1)$-th time; then $f(k)=\lfloor f(k-a)/2\rfloor+\lfloor f(k-b)/2\rfloor$ for $k\ge1$, so $f(sa+tb)>f(0)/2^{s+t}-2$; for large $N$ this forces $f\ge2$ on all integers beyond $ab-a-b$, i.e. infinitely many numbers, impossible.

imo-isl-2018-c7.prompt: Consider $2018$ pairwise crossing circles no three of which are concurrent. These circles subdivide the plane into regions bounded by circular *edges* that meet at *vertices*. Notice that there are an even number of vertices on each circle. Given the circle, alternately colour the vertices on that circle red and blue. In doing so for each circle, every vertex is coloured twice — once for each of the two circles that cross at that point. If the two colourings agree at a vertex, then it is assigned that colour; otherwise, it becomes yellow. Show that, if some circle contains at least $2061$ yellow points, then the vertices of some region are all yellow.
imo-isl-2018-c7.answer: Proof: if a circle has $k$ yellow points, parity lemmas (two crossing points of a pair of circles are both yellow or both not; every "triangle" of arcs has an odd number of yellow corners) force at least $\frac{k^2}2-(n-2)k+(n-1)(n-2)$ yellow vertices. If every region had a non-yellow vertex, each region would have at least two (non-yellow vertices alternate in colour around a region), giving at most $\frac{n(n-1)}2-1$ yellow vertices. Together $k\le n-2+\lfloor\sqrt{n-2}\rfloor=2060$.

imo-isl-2018-g2.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $P$ be a point such that $PB<PC$ and $PA$ is parallel to $BC$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be points on the lines $PB$ and $PC$, respectively, so that $B$ lies on the segment $PX$, $C$ lies on the segment $PY$, and $\angle PXM=\angle PYM$. Prove that the quadrilateral $APXY$ is cyclic.
imo-isl-2018-g2.answer: Proof: let $Z$ be the point of line $AM$ with $ZY\perp PC$. Then $P,A,Y,Z$ lie on the circle with diameter $PZ$; $CYZM$ is cyclic, so $\angle CZM=\angle CYM=\angle BXM$, and by symmetry $\angle BZM=\angle CZM$, so $B,X,Z,M$ are concyclic and $\angle PXZ=90^\circ$. Hence $X$ is on that circle too.

imo-isl-2018-g3.prompt:
A circle $\omega$ of radius $1$ is given. A collection $T$ of triangles is called *good*, if the following conditions hold:

(i) each triangle from $T$ is inscribed in $\omega$;

(ii) no two triangles from $T$ have a common interior point.

Determine all positive real numbers $t$ such that, for each positive integer $n$, there exists a good collection of $n$ triangles, each of perimeter greater than $t$.
imo-isl-2018-g3.answer: Exactly $0<t\le4$ (fan triangles from one end of a diameter all have perimeter $>4$; if $t=4+2\varepsilon$, Heron's formula gives each triangle area $\ge\sqrt{(2+\varepsilon)\varepsilon^3}$, so only boundedly many fit in the disc).

imo-isl-2018-g4.prompt: A point $T$ is chosen inside a triangle $ABC$. Let $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ be the reflections of $T$ in $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$, respectively. Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of the triangle $A_1B_1C_1$. The lines $A_1T$, $B_1T$, and $C_1T$ meet $\Omega$ again at $A_2$, $B_2$, and $C_2$, respectively. Prove that the lines $AA_2$, $BB_2$, and $CC_2$ are concurrent on $\Omega$.
imo-isl-2018-g4.answer: Proof (directed angles): $C$ is the circumcentre of $A_1TB_1$, which gives $\measuredangle(CA_1,CB)=\measuredangle(C_2A_1,C_2B_2)$ and similarly at $B$; so $A_1BC\sim A_1B_2C_2$, hence $A_1BB_2\sim A_1CC_2$, and the second intersection $K$ of $CC_2$ with $\Omega$ lies on $BB_2$ (and likewise on $AA_2$).

imo-isl-2018-g5.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcircle $\omega$ and incentre $I$. A line $\ell$ intersects the lines $AI$, $BI$, and $CI$ at points $D$, $E$, and $F$, respectively, distinct from the points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $I$. The perpendicular bisectors $x$, $y$, and $z$ of the segments $AD$, $BE$, and $CF$, respectively determine a triangle $\Theta$. Show that the circumcircle of the triangle $\Theta$ is tangent to $\omega$.
imo-isl-2018-g5.answer: Proof: $\Theta=XYZ$ is homothetic to $X_0Y_0Z_0$, where $X_0,Y_0,Z_0$ are the midpoints of arcs ($Y_0Z_0$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AI$, parallel to $x$). The reflections of $\ell$ in $x,y,z$ concur at a point $T\in\omega$, and an angle chase shows $T\in XX_0$, $YY_0$, $ZZ_0$; so $T$ is the centre of the homothety, which then maps $\omega$ to the circle $XYZ$ and fixes $T\in\omega$, giving tangency at $T$.

imo-isl-2018-g7.prompt: Let $O$ be the circumcentre, and $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $\Omega$, distinct from $A$, $B$, $C$, and their antipodes in $\Omega$. Denote the circumcentres of the triangles $AOP$, $BOP$, and $COP$ by $O_A$, $O_B$, and $O_C$, respectively. The lines $\ell_A$, $\ell_B$, and $\ell_C$ perpendicular to $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ pass through $O_A$, $O_B$, and $O_C$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle formed by $\ell_A$, $\ell_B$, and $\ell_C$ is tangent to the line $OP$.
imo-isl-2018-g7.answer: Proof (directed angles): with $L_A=\ell_B\cap\ell_C$ etc., the points $L_B,P,O_A,O_C$ are concyclic (and similarly), which shows $P$ lies on the circle $L_AL_BL_C$ and that $P,L_C,C$ (and $P,L_A,A$) are collinear; then $\measuredangle(OP,PL_A)=\measuredangle(PA,AO)=\measuredangle(PL_C,L_CL_A)$, the tangent–chord condition.

imo-isl-2018-n1.prompt: Determine all pairs $(n,k)$ of distinct positive integers such that there exists a positive integer $s$ for which the numbers of divisors of $sn$ and of $sk$ are equal.
imo-isl-2018-n1.answer: Exactly the pairs with $n\nmid k$ and $k\nmid n$ (if $n\mid k$, the divisors of $sn$ form a proper subset of those of $sk$; otherwise choose the exponents of $s$ so that the ratios $\frac{\alpha_i+\gamma_i+1}{\beta_i+\gamma_i+1}$ telescope to $1$).

imo-isl-2018-n2.prompt:
Let $n>1$ be a positive integer. Each cell of an $n\times n$ table contains an integer. Suppose that the following conditions are satisfied:

(i) Each number in the table is congruent to $1$ modulo $n$;

(ii) The sum of numbers in any row, as well as the sum of numbers in any column, is congruent to $n$ modulo $n^2$.

Let $R_i$ be the product of the numbers in the $i^{\text{th}}$ row, and $C_j$ be the product of the numbers in the $j^{\text{th}}$ column. Prove that the sums $R_1+\dots+R_n$ and $C_1+\dots+C_n$ are congruent modulo $n^4$.
imo-isl-2018-n2.answer: Proof: with $P$ the product of all entries, show $\sum R_i\equiv n-1+P\pmod{n^4}$ (and the same for columns): each $R_i\equiv1\pmod{n^2}$, so $P=\prod R_i\equiv1+\sum(R_i-1)\pmod{n^4}$.

imo-isl-2018-n3.prompt: Define the sequence $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots$ by $a_n=2^n+2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. Prove that there are infinitely many terms of the sequence which can be expressed as a sum of (two or more) distinct terms of the sequence, as well as infinitely many of those which cannot be expressed in such a way.
imo-isl-2018-n3.answer: Proof: with $S_{n-1}=a_0+\dots+a_{n-1}=2^n+2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}+2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}-3$, complements show $a_n$ is such a sum iff $2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}-3$ is a sum of distinct terms, and that $2^t-3$ and $2^{4t-6}-3$ behave alike. Starting from $2^3-3=a_0+a_1$ (yes) and $2^7-3=125$ (no) gives infinitely many of each.

imo-isl-2018-n5.prompt:
Four positive integers $x$, $y$, $z$, and $t$ satisfy the relations
$$xy-zt=x+y=z+t.$$
Is it possible that both $xy$ and $zt$ are perfect squares?

imo-isl-2018-n6.prompt: Let $f:\{1,2,3,\dots\}\to\{2,3,\dots\}$ be a function such that $f(m+n)\mid f(m)+f(n)$ for all pairs $m,n$ of positive integers. Prove that there exists a positive integer $c>1$ which divides all values of $f$.
imo-isl-2018-n6.answer: Proof: if $S_m=\{n:m\mid f(n)\}$ is infinite then it is the set of multiples of $\min S_m$. If $f$ is bounded, only finitely many primes occur; a prime dividing $f(N d_1\cdots d_k+1)$ for large $N$ then divides every value. If $f$ is unbounded, "peaks" $p$ satisfy $f(k)+f(p-k)=f(p)$, and peaks with equal $f$ mod $a=f(1)$ show $S_a$ is infinite, so $f(1)$ divides all values.

imo-isl-2018-n7.prompt:
Let $n\ge2018$ be an integer, and let $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n,b_1,b_2,\dots,b_n$ be pairwise distinct positive integers not exceeding $5n$. Suppose that the sequence
$$\frac{a_1}{b_1},\ \frac{a_2}{b_2},\ \dots,\ \frac{a_n}{b_n}$$
forms an arithmetic progression. Prove that the terms of the sequence are equal.
imo-isl-2018-n7.answer:
Proof: if the common difference is $c/d
e0$ in lowest terms, then for each prime $p\mid d$ the indices $i$ with $
u_p(b_i)<
u_p(d)$ lie in one residue class mod $p$. This forces $d$ to have only prime factors $2,3,5$, and then $d\mid b_i$ for at least $8$ indices in every block of $30$. Since at least $n/2$ terms lie in $(0,10]$, $d> rac{n-2}{20}$, and these multiples of $d$ would exceed $5n$.
